correctness.rationale: In GP(10,2) the exhaustive anchored DFS lists all 30 Hamilton cycles (two rooted orientations per unlabelled cycle, one retained). Independently 36 recursively enumerated perfect matchings have 30 connected complementary two-factors. Every one of 435 cycle pairs is tested for a single alternating 8-cycle. There are 60 switches, degree four at each state, connected exchange graph and diameter four. Antipodal vertex shift by five induces 15 pairs and an opposite-color involution. Quotient triangle incidence yields ten Petersen vertices explicitly mapped to KG(5,2), proving the quotient is L(P); double lift proves the full graph is K2 x L(P). Every shorter admissible alternating cycle would be an even 4- or 6-cycle, neither present. Exact scripts and certificate are embedded.

evidence: Sierksma 1998 explicitly studies interchange graphs of tours in complete graphs K_n (https://research.rug.nl/en/publications/interchange-graphs-and-the-hamilton-cycle-polytope/).
Takaoka 2018 changes two cycle edges at a time, i.e. four edges in symmetric difference (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327708735_Complexity_of_Hamiltonian_Cycle_Reconfiguration).

Schwenk 1989 gives Hamilton cycle counts in GP(n,2), not their shortest-switch metric or quotient (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/220077067_Enumeration_of_Hamiltonian_cycles_in_certain_generalized_Petersen_graphs).
broader_coverage.reasoning: The Hamilton-cycle count theorems are strictly weaker than a full adjacency relation and graph isomorphism. The complete-graph interchange theorem cannot imply induced restricted graph adjacency in D without a separate argument; it does not analyze D. The two-edge switch operation in Takaoka has no moves in this girth-five graph and therefore cannot subsume the claimed eight-cycle-switch connectivity.

originality.rationale: Schwenk 1989 establishes the count of Hamiltonian cycles of GP(10,2); Hopkins 2004 establishes uniqueness up to full symmetry; neither describes the exact 8-edge switch graph or its antipodal quotient. The relevant published Hamilton-tour interchange work is for complete graphs, while 2018 two-edge switches are impossible on the dodecahedral graph. Full accessible Schwenk and Hopkins text was read and compared by mathematical implication; no covering claim was located. Indexed and web searches are negative evidence only, not proof of novelty. Risk: old unindexed icosian or graph-transformation literature may encode the same 30-vertex cover.
residual_risks: A historically unpublished or unindexed exact description of shortest dodecahedral Hamilton-cycle exchanges could be equivalent to the proposed graph isomorphism.
The Sierksma full paper was not read, although its complete-graph domain is manifestly different; the comparison is based on institutional metadata and abstract.
No formal independent external scholarly validation of the novelty search or the proof was performed.

value.rationale: The Icosian dodecahedron is the historical benchmark for Hamilton cycles, already known to have 30 tours. Determining whether its tours can be locally transformed without losing Hamiltonicity is a natural distinct problem. The minimal connected alternating-cycle threshold eight, exact mobility and diameter, and interpretation as a bipartite double cover of the Petersen line graph identify previously undescribed structure and tie the move graph to the antipodal geometry; these are motivated invariant facts, not arbitrary parameter slices or a routine recount of 30 known cycles.
